A note first

Welcome, Our Dearest Guests

Welcome to our desert wedding — thank you for travelling all this way to stand with us under a very wide sky. We met on a road trip, and we are getting married where the light turns gold every single evening.

Everything you need is on this page: times, addresses, where to stay, what to wear, and the RSVP at the bottom. If anything is unclear, message us. We would rather answer twice than have you guess once.

— Maya & Arjun

How we got here

Our Story

Scroll sideways through four moments.

2020 — A Road Trip

We met on the open road

Maya’s car broke down outside a desert town; Arjun stopped, fixed nothing, but stayed for coffee. The coffee lasted three hours. The road trip never really ended.

2021–2024 — The Desert Habit

Weekends under wide skies

Every free weekend became a desert drive — cacti, sunsets, and terrible playlists sung loudly. Arjun navigates; Maya chooses the music. The habit never stopped.

March 2026 — At Golden Hour

He asked as the sun went down

On a warm evening at this very lodge, as the sky turned terracotta, Arjun asked properly. Maya said yes, then made him ask again so the sunset could be in the photo.

3 October 2027 — Today, With You

Now we want you in the room

Desert light, string lights, and the people who made us who we are. That is the whole plan — and the only thing missing is you.

Plan your trip

Venue, Travel & Stay

Flying in? Start here, then pick a hotel that fits your budget.

The Venue

Saguaro Desert Lodge, Arizona — our recommended base if you want one place for the whole celebration.

Open in Google Maps

Getting Here

Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport (PHX) is the nearest airport. Allow about 1 hour 30 minutes by car to the lodge in normal traffic — book your ride in advance for the main evening.

Parking & Shuttle

Parking is available at the venue where noted in the FAQ. There is no arranged shuttle between hotels, so please plan a ride for each evening and pre-book for late returns.

Where to Stay

Price bands are indicative for planning only — please confirm live rates when you book.

Budget — desert motels & inns
Simple desert stays near the lodge road; allow a drive to the venue.
Mid-range — Saguaro Town Hotel
A twenty-minute drive from the lodge, with a pool for the morning after.
Premium — Saguaro Desert Lodge (venue hotel)
Stay where the wedding is — desert sunsets from your door.

Travelling with children or elderly family? Tell us in the RSVP message and we will help you choose the most comfortable option.

What to wear

Dress Code

Boho formal in earthy tones: terracotta, sand, rust and cream. Flowing fabrics welcome; please avoid heels on desert ground — flat sandals or wedges are safest.

Terracotta — aim for this
Sand — aim for this
Clay — welcome
Dune — welcome

A Note on Gifts

Your presence is the gift — truly. If you still wish to give, a contribution towards our honeymoon is welcome, and we will share details personally with anyone who asks. There is no online registry or payment link on this page, by design.

Good to know

Questions, Answered

Tap a question to open it.

Yes — children are welcome. Please include them in your guest count so we can seat and cater for them. The welcome evening is the most relaxed night for families.

Only if your invitation names a plus-one, or you have confirmed one with us directly. If unsure, write it in the RSVP message and we will confirm — seating is planned by name.

Parking is available at the lodge car park. Arrive by 5:00 PM for the sunset ceremony — the desert road is unlit after dark, so plan your return ride.

Boho formal, earthy tones. Avoid heels on sand and gravel; flat sandals or wedges are essential. Bring a layer — desert evenings cool fast after sunset.

No gift is expected — your presence is the gift. If you wish to give, a honeymoon contribution is welcome; ask us personally for details.

October in Arizona is warm by day and cool at night. The ceremony is outdoors on sandy ground — flat shoes are essential, and a shawl for after sunset is wise.
